items.title: File Berkeley County business personal property return
items.authority: Berkeley County County Auditor or SC Department of Revenue
items.description: South Carolina business personal property returns are due the last day of the fourth month after the accounting period closes (April 30 for calendar-year filers), to the county auditor or, for retail and sales-tax businesses, the SCDOR. The county's own page was not individually confirmed; the state's guidance applies and the return goes to the county.

note: Berkeley County's hospitality tax rules were not found.

items.title: File Charleston County business personal property return
items.description: South Carolina business personal property returns are due the last day of the fourth month after the accounting period closes (April 30 for calendar-year filers), to the county auditor or, for retail and sales-tax businesses, the SCDOR.

items.title: File the Charleston County hospitality tax return
items.description: Restaurants pay a 2% hospitality tax in Charleston County, reported to the county by the 20th of the month after the sales month with a 25% penalty for late remittance. This comes from a town ordinance that follows the county's Chapter 24; the county's own page for unincorporated restaurants was not found.

note: Charleston County's Revenue Collections Division collects a 2% local accommodations fee (Ordinance 910), also on behalf of the cities of Charleston, North Charleston and Folly Beach, but its return due date was not found.

items.title: File Greenville County business personal property return
items.authority: Greenville County County Auditor or SC Department of Revenue
items.description: South Carolina business personal property returns are due the last day of the fourth month after the accounting period closes (April 30 for calendar-year filers), to the county auditor or, for retail and sales-tax businesses, the SCDOR. The county's own page was not individually confirmed; the state's guidance applies and the return goes to the county.

items.title: File the Greenville County hospitality tax return
items.description: Restaurants and bars owe the county's 2% local hospitality tax on prepared food and drink. Remittance is due at the Treasurer's Office or postmarked by the 20th of the month after the reporting period (next business day if the 20th is a weekend or postal holiday). The county assigns monthly or quarterly filing from estimated sales (monthly above about $2,500 a month on an older FAQ). A 5% penalty is added for each month late. Register with Financial Operations first (864-467-7567).

note: Greenville also has a county accommodations fee return with the Treasurer; its due date was not found.

items.title: File the Horry County lodging tax return
items.description: Accommodations remittance forms and payment are due by the 20th of the month after the reporting period (monthly, quarterly or yearly per account); a zero return must still be signed and mailed. Register your account with the Hospitality Fee Department (843-915-5620); unincorporated short-term rentals also need a county business license and the state forms ST-388, ST-3T and ST-389.

appliesWhen.description: Operates a hotel, motel or short-term rental

items.title: File the Horry County hospitality tax return
items.authority: Horry County Treasurer, Hospitality Fee Department
items.description: Food and beverage sales outside city limits pay the county's 2.5% hospitality fee, due the 20th of the month after the reporting period; payments after the 20th incur a penalty. Five cities including Myrtle Beach and Conway replaced the county fee inside their limits. Phone 843-915-5620.

items.title: File Richland County business personal property return
items.description: South Carolina business personal property returns are due the last day of the fourth month after the accounting period closes (April 30 for calendar-year filers), to the county auditor or, for retail and sales-tax businesses, the SCDOR.

items.title: File the Richland County hospitality tax return
items.description: The hospitality tax is 2% in unincorporated areas and several cities (1% in Eastover and the county part of Irmo). Remit by the 20th of each month for the prior month's collections, with the signed voucher and the state ST-3 for the same period; a return postmarked the next business day counts if the 20th is a weekend or postal holiday. New businesses file monthly for their first twelve months. Late: 5% per month.

items.title: File the Spartanburg County hospitality tax return
items.authority: Spartanburg County Treasurer, Hospitality Tax Division
items.description: Businesses outside the City of Spartanburg and other municipalities pay the county hospitality tax by the 20th of the month after the sales period (next business day if the county is closed). Remittance is monthly when the average monthly tax is over $50, quarterly at $25 to $50 and annually under $25. A 5% penalty is added each month until paid.

items.title: File York County business personal property return
items.description: South Carolina business personal property returns are due the last day of the fourth month after the accounting period closes (April 30 for calendar-year filers), to the county auditor or, for retail and sales-tax businesses, the SCDOR.

items.title: File the York County hospitality tax return
items.description: The hospitality tax is 2% in unincorporated York County (1% inside Hickory Grove, McConnells, Sharon and Smyrna). Pay at the Treasurer's Office or postmark by the 20th of the following month, with the ST-3 attached; filing is monthly when the estimated average tax is over $50 a month. A 5% penalty applies for each month late.
